answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying every identity to a costly, verifiable voyage of work: each agent must complete a chain of real tasks whose results are checked by independent peers before it earns reputation. A lightweight cipher challenge proves the agent holds its own key, while a walnut-hard proof-of-effort, small enough to be cheap once yet ruinous to fake a thousand times, makes mass account creation unprofitable. Reputation then accrues slowly and is lost fast on misbehavior, so one honest history beats a thousand fresh shells.
